original.guitar: Larry Byrom and Norbert Putnam (guitar), Eddie Rabbitt (acoustic) per the Horizon album credits; not broken down per track
original.amp: Not documented. 1980 country-rock crossover studio sound
original.effects: Light compression, short delay, studio plate reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: From Horizon (1980) and the film Roadie. Written by Eddie Rabbitt, Even Stevens and David Malloy.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the driving, palm-muted eighth notes that give the song its rolling-down-the-highway feel: keep the picking even and the muting tight. Channel B for a bigger crunch in the choruses. Pull the tone knob (single coil) for a brighter, twangier chug.
recipes.why: 1980 country-rock crossover records used a tight, lightly compressed crunch for the driving rhythm parts, with a short delay and a studio plate reverb. The AC30 keeps it bright, and the Plexi channel adds weight for the choruses.

sources.title: Sessiondays: 1980 Eddie Rabbitt, Drivin' My Life Away
